correctness.rationale: Imamura's finite BMI theorem identifies such algebras with finite idempotent associative semigroups having the designated left identities. For any such band, each left identity e satisfies ex=x=x(ex), so Y is nonempty. Associativity and yx=x(yx) show closure: (yz)x=y(zx)=y(x(zx))=(yx)(zx)=x(y(zx)); substituting x=y into z's defining identity gives yzy=zy. In every band the failures of yx=xyx and xy=yxy are equivalent by multiplying on the right and idempotence, so a non-Y point has a distinct non-Y witness; a singleton complement is impossible. For any unital right-regular band R add a disjoint left-zero ideal U of at least two elements with ru=ur=u and uv=u; words containing U evaluate to their first U factor, ensuring associativity, identity and Y=R. This proves the exact Σ_n={1..n-2,n} for n>=3, with n<=2 full locus; no inference from small finite tests. Independently enumerated all labeled bands through four elements with a prescribed left unit, obtaining 1,2,9,84 and corresponding Y-size spectra {1},{2},{1,3},{1,2,4}.
